title: Pullback and tensor product of invertible modules, and their fibres

source.place: Modules, Lemma Tag 01CD (lemma-tensor-product-pullback: f^*(F (x) G) = f^*F (x) f^*G), Lemma Tag 0B8L (lemma-pullback-invertible) with Tag 01C8 (lemma-pullback-locally-free), Lemma Tag 01CT (lemma-constructions-invertible (1): tensor products of invertible modules are invertible), Section Tag 01CA (symmetry and associativity of the tensor product); for (3): Sheaves, Lemma Tag 0098 (sheaves-lemma-stalk-pullback-modules: (f^*F)_x = F_{f(x)} (x)_{O_{Y,f(x)}} O_{X,x}) and Modules, Lemma Tag 01CB (lemma-stalk-tensor-product: (F (x) G)_y = F_y (x) G_y)

proof.text: *The fibre $\mathcal L(y)$ is one-dimensional.* Let $y\in Y$. By [def-sc-invertible-module] there are an open $V\ni y$ and an isomorphism $\mathcal L|_V\cong\mathcal O_V$; the stalk at $y$ of a sheaf is the stalk at $y$ of its restriction to an open containing $y$, so $\mathcal L_y\cong\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ as $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$-modules, and $\mathcal L(y)=\mathcal L_y\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,y}}\kappa(y)\cong\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is a one-dimensional $\kappa(y)$-vector space. The same applies to every invertible module on any scheme, in particular (after (1)) to $f^*\mathcal L$ and $\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M$.

source.place: Modules, Section 17.14 (Tag 01C5, locally free sheaves; Definition Tag 01C6) and Lemma Tag 0B8M (an invertible module on a locally ringed space has stalks $\mathcal L_x\cong\mathcal O_{X,x}$)

proof.text: *(1), pullback.* $f^*\mathcal L$ is an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-invertible]: if $\mathcal L|_V\cong\mathcal O_V$ then $(f^*\mathcal L)|_{f^{-1}V}\cong\mathcal O_{f^{-1}V}$, and the opens $f^{-1}V$ cover $X$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma Tag 01C8 (lemma-pullback-locally-free) and Lemma Tag 0B8L (lemma-pullback-invertible)

proof.text: *(1), tensor product.* $\mathcal L\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal M$ is an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module by [lem-pc-tensor-dual-invertible] (applied on the scheme $Y$ to $\mathcal L,\mathcal M$; the argument there: on an open $V$ trivializing both, $(\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M)|_V\cong\mathcal O_V\otimes\mathcal O_V\cong\mathcal O_V$). This is a generic tool lemma of sec-picard-framework (unit sk-thm-picard-hilb-curves), used as a black box.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 17.25.6 (Tag 01CT, label lemma-constructions-invertible, (1)); also Lemma Tag 01CE (lemma-tensor-product-permanence, (7))

proof.text: *(2), pullback of a tensor product.* By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor] with $\mathcal F=\mathcal L$, $\mathcal G=\mathcal M$ there is an isomorphism $f^*(\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M)\cong f^*\mathcal L\otimes f^*\mathcal M$, natural in $\mathcal L,\mathcal M$, sending $f^*(s\otimes t)$ to $f^*s\otimes f^*t$.

*(2), composition.* Let $g:W\to X$. The isomorphism $\theta:g^*f^*\cong(f\circ g)^*$ of [def-pc-module-pullback] is the one given by uniqueness of left adjoints (Stacks Tag 0097: $(f\circ g)_*=f_*g_*$, and $g^*f^*$ is left adjoint to $f_*g_*$ by composing the adjunctions of Tag 0096; in Mathlib `Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp`, characterized by `conjugateEquiv_pullbackComp_inv`). Write $\eta^f:\mathrm{id}\to f_*f^*$, $\eta^g$, $\eta^{fg}$ for the units; the unit of the composite adjunction $g^*f^*\dashv f_*g_*$ is $\varepsilon_{\mathcal L}=f_*(\eta^g_{f^*\mathcal L})\circ\eta^f_{\mathcal L}:\mathcal L\to f_*g_*g^*f^*\mathcal L$. That $\theta$ corresponds to the identity of $(f\circ g)_*=f_*g_*$ means exactly $(f\circ g)_*(\theta_{\mathcal L})\circ\varepsilon_{\mathcal L}=\eta^{fg}_{\mathcal L}$ (the transformation of left adjoints conjugate to a transformation of right adjoints is the unique one compatible with the units). Evaluate on $s\in\mathcal L(V)$: $\eta^f_{\mathcal L}(s)=f^*s\in(f^*\mathcal L)(f^{-1}V)$, $f_*(\eta^g_{f^*\mathcal L})(f^*s)=g^*f^*s\in(g^*f^*\mathcal L)(g^{-1}f^{-1}V)$, so $\theta(g^*f^*s)=\eta^{fg}_{\mathcal L}(s)=(f\circ g)^*s$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 6.26.2 (Tag 0096, adjunction $f^*\dashv f_*$ for modules) and Lemma Tag 0097 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules: $(g\circ f)_*=g_*f_*$ and $(g\circ f)^*\cong f^*g^*$, by uniqueness of adjoints)

proof.text: *(2), symmetry and reordering.* By [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-symmetric-monoidal] the symmetry $c:\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M\to\mathcal M\otimes\mathcal L$, $s\otimes t\mapsto t\otimes s$, is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules, and for invertible $\mathcal L_1,\dots,\mathcal L_n$ and a permutation $\pi$ the same node gives the isomorphism $\mathcal L_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal L_n\to\mathcal L_{\pi^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal L_{\pi^{-1}(n)}$ moving the $i$-th factor to position $\pi(i)$, $s_1\otimes\cdots\otimes s_n\mapsto s_{\pi^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes s_{\pi^{-1}(n)}$ (a composite of associators and of symmetries of adjacent factors, the adjacent transpositions generating the symmetric group).

source.place: Modules, Section 17.16 (Tag 01CA): symmetry and associativity of $\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}$

proof.text:
*(3), fibre of a pullback.* Let $x\in X$, $y=f(x)$, and let $\varphi=f^\sharp_x:\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$, a local homomorphism, so the composite $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}\to\kappa(x)$ factors through $\kappa(y)$, giving $\kappa(y)\to\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback], $(f^*\mathcal L)_x\cong\mathcal L_y\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,y}}\mathcal O_{X,x}$ with $(f^*s)_x\mapsto s_y\otimes1$. Hence
$(f^*\mathcal L)(x)=(f^*\mathcal L)_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\kappa(x)\cong\mathcal L_y\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,y}}\kappa(x)\cong(\mathcal L_y\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,y}}\kappa(y))\otimes_{\kappa(y)}\kappa(x)=\mathcal L(y)\otimes_{\kappa(y)}\kappa(x)$,
by associativity of base change ($(N\otimes_AB)\otimes_BC=N\otimes_AC$ for ring maps $A\to B\to C$, applied to $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}\to\kappa(x)$ and to $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to\kappa(y)\to\kappa(x)$). Following $s_y\otimes1$ through these identifications: $(f^*s)(x)=(s_y\otimes1)\otimes1\mapsto s_y\otimes1\mapsto(s_y\otimes1)\otimes1=s(y)\otimes1$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 6.26.4 (Tag 0098, label lemma-stalk-pullback-modules); the base-change identities from Algebra, Lemma Tag 00D2 (lemma-tensor-with-bimodule: $(M\otimes_AN)\otimes_BP\cong M\otimes_A(N\otimes_BP)$), literature/stacks-project/algebra.tex

proof.text: *(3), fibre of a tensor product.* Let $y\in Y$, $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, $k=\kappa(y)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-tensor], $(\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M)_y\cong\mathcal L_y\otimes_A\mathcal M_y$ with $(s\otimes t)_y\mapsto s_y\otimes t_y$. For $A$-modules $P,Q$ the map $(P\otimes_AQ)\otimes_Ak\to(P\otimes_Ak)\otimes_k(Q\otimes_Ak)$, $(p\otimes q)\otimes1\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes(q\otimes1)$, is an isomorphism (both sides are $P\otimes_AQ\otimes_Ak$ by associativity and commutativity of $\otimes_A$, using $k\otimes_kk=k$). Hence $(\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M)(y)\cong\mathcal L(y)\otimes_{\kappa(y)}\mathcal M(y)$ with $(s\otimes t)(y)=(s_y\otimes t_y)\otimes1\mapsto s(y)\otimes t(y)$ [def-weil-residue-field].

source.place: Modules, Lemma 17.16.1 (Tag 01CB, label lemma-stalk-tensor-product); the base-change identity from Algebra, Lemmas Tag 00D0 (lemma-transitive, associativity), 00CY (lemma-flip-tensor-product) and 00D2 (lemma-tensor-with-bimodule), literature/stacks-project/algebra.tex

split_report.summary: Split into 8 steps following Stacks: fibre dimension (elementary from the definition), (1) pullback via new node lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-invertible (Stacks 01C8/0B8L; slopmaster2 Lean IsInvertible.pullback is sorry-free) and tensor product via the existing tool lem-pc-tensor-dual-invertible (Stacks 01CT(1)); (2) f^*(L(x)M) via new node lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor (01CD), composition with sections written out from the conjugate characterization of the isomorphism of def-pc-module-pullback (0096; Mathlib pullbackComp/conjugateEquiv_pullbackComp_inv), symmetry/reordering via new node lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-symmetric-monoidal (01CA, 05NA); (3) fibres via new nodes lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback (0098) and lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-tensor (01CB), with the base-change identities written out. Statement kept; a sentence fixing the meaning of f^*s and s(x)t (unit of the adjunction, image under sheafification) was added, and stmt_deps extended by def-pc-module-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-residue-field. The source place in the statement misattributed 01CB (stalk of a tensor product, not tensor of invertibles) and 0B8K (invertible iff L(x)N = O); tensor of invertibles is 01CT. Mathlib has neither a tensor product of sheaves of modules nor invertible modules on schemes (three kinds of search recorded on the new nodes).
